### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class), flow_route (symbol, a field of interface ApprovalRequestRow))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `293ab7ad9c98d86695993dfff008f3a57f12cf0e` — the merge of head `99ab892be2124f2684739442beead6ade367e638` into base `49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 293ab7ad9c98d86695993dfff008f3a57f12cf0e && git checkout 293ab7ad9c98d86695993dfff008f3a57f12cf0e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2 99ab892be2124f2684739442beead6ade367e638 && git checkout -B drift-repro 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2 && git merge --no-ff 99ab892be2124f2684739442beead6ade367e638

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1f6480a2c9053de0ea8c75d7ffdeb2797b2897b4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-route.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, ui/apps/console/src/services/approvalsApi.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useRecordApprovals.ts
Security-touching: yes

Inputs read: card #35863 (body and all four comments: triage 7042462136, unblock 7042569075, claim 7146092596, dev report 7147715077; no ruling and no earlier record on the card), PR #37148 body and file list, the net diff `517e4153..1f6480a2` (23 files), and the 74 check-runs on the head. The four implementing files were each confirmed against the diff: `approval-route.ts` holds the rule (`routeOutcome`, `flowRoute`), `approval-service.ts` reads the run state (`attachFlowRoute`, `runHasEnded`), and the two UI files are type mirrors of the served member. `ApprovalStepLine.tsx` and `ApprovalDecisionPanel.tsx` render the member and were read to judge the contract's first consumer; they, the tests, the changeset prose, the docs page and the locale bundles are the lane seat's accept.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: one optional member, `outcome`, on the exported contract type `ApprovalRequestRow['flow_route']` in `@objectstack/spec/contracts`. Type-only, response-side, additive; no new export, no zod schema, no authorable key, no accept-set change. Right. `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:export-origins`), `Spec property liveness` and `TypeScript Type Check` all concluded success on the head.
- `routeOutcome` and the fifth `flowRoute` parameter (`runEnded = false`) are module exports of `approval-route.ts` only; `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/index.ts` re-exports nothing from that module, so the package's public surface does not move. Right.
- Served wire shape: `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/ID` (and the write echoes that share `loadRequest`) gain `flow_route.outcome` on decided rows. List reads are untouched: `attachFlowSteps` stays single-read enrichment. Right.
- Check-runs on the head: 74, none failed and none pending; every conclusion is success or skipped. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core`, `Test UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes` and `Check Documentation Links` are success. The skipped ones are opt-in or queue-only jobs (upgrade harness, packed-tarball smoke, queue verdicts, temporal conformance, dogfood matrix and CLI, UI published artifacts, the schedule gate, and the superseded duplicate `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` runs).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/35863-decided-route-outcome.md` moves `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/console`, each at `patch`. The diff publishes from exactly those five packages. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes. Under the AGENTS.md rule (the level follows the protocol kind alone; `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol widening ships `patch`), `patch` is the right level for an additive optional member on a served contract type. `Check Changeset` concluded success.

Clause-②: yes — declared identically in the PR body and the changeset body; the change is an additive widening of a published contract type, no `(narrowing)` arm applies and none is claimed. Agreed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Dev report `security_findings: none`: not agreed. The new member serves facts taken from a request the reader may be unable to read; see S1 below. This is the reason for `Security-touching: yes`.
- Dev out-of-scope note 1 (the line does not name who holds the later step): agreed, and it is the right call. Approver names of a later request are request content; leaving them out keeps the disclosure to node, label, status and run end.
- Dev out-of-scope note 2 (a run that fails after an approval reads `ended` with `status: 'approved'`): accepted as described; the contract says `status` is the last decision, which stays true. It does not cover the child-run case in M1, which is a different defect.
- Claim widening (i18n bundles, console type mirror, docs page): recorded on the claim by the seat's edit; nothing for this review beyond the two type mirrors, which are in Scope.
- Escalated to the seat and maintainer: whether a participant of an earlier request may learn the status of a later request of the same run that they cannot read. The live tree cites ruling 5299823744 on #8652 ("request content stays behind `approvalsVisibleToReaders`", `getRecordLock` docblock). That ruling's text is not among this review's inputs, so this record does not decide the question; it records that the PR decided it silently. The precedent in the same field is `passedSteps` (#26668), which already serves "this earlier node was approved" from rows read as the system.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. `outcome` adds no read of `sys_approval_request`: it reuses the one run-scoped `find` the route already makes (`where: { flow_run_id }`, five fields, `limit: 1000`), and picks the latest row in memory from that bounded set. No new id materialisation, no in-app join. The only new I/O is one `automation.getRun` per single read, on decided rows only; no N+1, since list reads never reach `attachFlowRoute`.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` (hits).** The member's shape matches the card's option 2 and the claim's stated shape, plus `ended`, whose addition the PR explains and which the contract documents. The sentences on `step`, `status`, the pending-first rule, the later-round rule and the three absence cases agree with `routeOutcome` and `runHasEnded` line for line, with the exceptions below. Break attempts that held: several later requests (latest by `created_at`, pending first; two or more pending gives no outcome); a run that ended with no later request (`status` is this request's own, `ended: true`); an unreadable run (`getRun` absent, null or throwing reads as not ended, so no outcome without a later row); a request sent back and waiting on a resubmit (no later row, run live, no outcome); a later round of the same node (counted, as documented); cost per route (one `getRun`, no extra query).

M1 (must-fix) — `ended` is read off the request's own `flow_run_id`, and a child run's end is served as the end of the record's approval. An approval node takes its run id from `$runId` (`approval-node.ts:173-192`), and a `subflow` or `map` body runs as its own child run with its own id, linked upward only by `$parentRunId` (`subflow-node.ts:103-110`, `map-node.ts:250`); `approval-service.ts` already treats this as a supported shape (the subflow-parent strand handling around `takeSubflowParentStrand`). For a request hosted in such a child run, the child run completes as soon as its last approval is decided, so `runHasEnded` answers true and the route serves `outcome: { status: 'approved', ended: true }` while the parent run goes on, possibly to further approval requests on the same record under the parent's run id (rows `routeOutcome` never sees, because it reads one `flow_run_id`). The contract sentence "`ended` — the run has stopped and will never resume, so `status` is the last decision the record's approval took" is then false, and the first consumer draws "The approval ended here" for an approval that has not ended. This breaks the member's own rule ("read off the request's flow run and never guessed") and the route's existing treatment of the same node types on the forward walk, where `stepsAhead` stops at `subflow` / `map` / `loop` with `ahead: 'undecided'` rather than claim an end. Fix direction: a run that has a parent is not "ended" for this purpose (serve no `ended: true`, hence no outcome when there is no later row), or the contract narrows `ended` to the request's own run and the UI stops calling that the approval's end; either way with a pin for an approval inside a subflow. Read from source, not run.

S1 (should-fix) — the new member crosses the request-visibility boundary and neither the contract nor the service says so. `visibleRequestIds` admits a reader to a request as its submitter, a current approver or someone who acted on it; a step-1 approver is therefore a reader of the step-1 request and, with the record-reader tier off, not of the step-2 request. `attachFlowRoute` reads the run's rows under `SYSTEM_CTX`, and its docblock justifies that with "the route names steps and their labels, which `flow_steps` already served to the same reader". After this change the same system read also serves the later request's `status` (pending, approved, rejected, returned, recalled, cancelled) and whether the run ended, which `flow_steps` never served: the stated justification no longer covers what the read serves. What is disclosed is narrow (node id, label, status, run end; no request id, no approvers, no comments, no payload) and the card asks for exactly this, so this is graded should-fix rather than a refusal: the `outcome` docblock in the contract must state its audience (every reader of this request, whether or not they can read the later request) and what it deliberately leaves out, and the `attachFlowRoute` docblock must state the new disclosure and its reason in place of the labels-only sentence. Whether the disclosure itself is permitted under the #8652 ruling is escalated in ③.

Nits (no effect on the verdict):
- N1 — `ended: true` beside `status: 'pending'` is reachable: a later request still pending on a run that has already turned terminal, in the window before `releaseDeadRunRequests` recalls it. The contract's "so `status` is the last decision" does not hold for that pair, and the UI then says "waiting for a decision". The sentence could say "when `status` is not `pending`".
- N2 — "later" is `created_at` after this request's `created_at`, not after its decision. A sibling request of the same run opened while this one was still pending would read as "went on to". The `parallel` node refuses a durable pause inside a branch, so no reachable case was found; noted only because the contract's parallel carve-out counts pending later rows and a single one passes it.
- N3 — the two UI mirrors type `outcome.status` as `string` where the contract says `ApprovalStatus`. Consistent with how both files already type the row's own `status` (a union widened by `string`); accepted deviation.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-route.ts`.** `routeOutcome` agrees with the contract sentence by sentence apart from M1's premise, which it inherits through `runEnded`: later rows are same-run rows other than this one with a later `created_at`; more than one pending returns undefined; one pending wins; otherwise the latest; with no later row it returns this request's own status only when the run ended. `flowRoute` attaches it on non-pending rows only, so a pending route never carries it, as the contract says. The row filter does not check `flow_run_id` itself and relies on the caller's run-scoped read, as `passedSteps` does and documents.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`.** `runHasEnded` uses the dead-run sweep's `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES`, derived from the total `RUN_STATUS_LIVENESS` map, and degrades every unreadable case to false, which matches the contract's "the run's state cannot be read" absence arm. It is asked only for decided rows. Its defect is M1 (it cannot tell a child run from a root run); its docblock gap is S1.

**`ui/apps/console/src/services/approvalsApi.ts`, `ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useRecordApprovals.ts`.** Both mirror the member's three fields and optionality exactly; the `useRecordApprovals` comment restates the contract correctly. Only N3 applies. Both inherit whatever M1's fix changes in the meaning of `ended`.

Open on this head: M1 (must-fix), S1 (should-fix).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-x90m5y`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgv2LZN1W2qSYTZvYs`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head 1f6480a2 · 2026-11-24T23:51Z

L1: REWORK (L1-w, zone wf-B)
Head-sha: `1f6480a2c9053de0ea8c75d7ffdeb2797b2897b4`

The L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this head is **FAIL**, comment 7147867236. Its M1 (must-fix) and S1 (should-fix) are adopted here as they stand, and the fix round answers them there. I checked M1 against the tree: an approval node takes `$runId` (`approval-node.ts`), and `subflow` starts a child run linked upward only by `$parentRunId` (`service-automation/src/builtin/subflow-node.ts`). So `runHasEnded(row.flow_run_id)` reads the child run's end as the end of the record's approval. One L1 finding of my own follows.

### Should-fix (L1)

**S2. Three texts say `outcome` is absent when the run cannot be read, but the code serves it.** The spec docblock ("Absent when … the run's state cannot be read"), the changeset ("`outcome` is absent when … the run cannot be read") and `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` ("`outcome` is left out when … a run that cannot be read") all list an unreadable run as its own reason for absence. `runHasEnded` answers `false` for no `getRun`, no run, or a throw, and `routeOutcome` still returns `{ step, status, ended: false }` whenever a later request row exists. Example: step 2 rejected and the run in fact ended, but `getRun` throws. The route serves `ended: false`, and the line reads "Went on to Finance: Rejected" instead of "…, then ended: Rejected". That `false` is a guess, against the member's own "never guessed". The plugin docblock does say "A run that cannot be read is not ended: the outcome then rests on the rows alone", so code and plugin doc agree, and the published texts are the ones that are wrong.
- Fix, either way: (a) make the three texts say an unreadable run is absent only when no later request was opened, and define `ended: false` as "not known to have stopped"; or (b) serve no `outcome` when the run cannot be read. Choose together with M1's fix, which also changes what `ended` means.

### Read and found right (head 1f6480a2)

- `l1-face.mjs --pr 37148`: 13 items clean. Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #35863` binds only this card, `Clause-②: yes` / `Metadata-protocol: none` match claim 7146092596 as amended. The changeset names all five published packages moved: spec, plugin-approvals, app-shell, i18n, console. `patch` is right for `Metadata-protocol: none` (AGENTS.md: a non-protocol widening ships `patch`). All checks are green and nothing is pending. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Scope.** All 23 files sit inside the amended claim surface. The `import '@object-ui/plugin-detail'` added to the existing step-line test is a declared dependency of `@object-ui/app-shell` (it warms a lazy import before the clocked cases) and inside the claim's app-shell pins.
- **`Fixes` is right, once the findings close.** The card's two pins are present. Step 1 decided with step 2 pending is shown in the integration test and the panel test. The last step decided reading "ended" is shown too. The card's "and who holds it now" is left out on purpose (the PR's acceptance notes). The card's own option 2 ("a single outcome") does not ask for it either.
- **Reads.** The outcome reuses the route's existing run-scoped `find` and adds one `getRun`, only for decided rows and only on the single-request read (`attachFlowSteps`: "list reads skip it"). There is no per-row fan-out.
- **UI.** One line below the `ol`, outside the list, so assistive tech does not count it as a step. It is drawn only with `decided` and never on a pending route (pinned). The four new `approvalsInbox` rows are in all 11 locale packs, zh-Hans and en included, and a pin covers every pack. The keys do not collide with the existing `outcomeApprove` / `outcomeReject`.
- **Tests.** The two ablation runs fail exactly the new pins: `flowRoute` outcome forced off gives 4 failed, and `runHasEnded` forced false gives 3 failed. The decision panel hand-off removed gives 4 failed. Each was restored.

### Path to ACCEPT

The card thread fixes L2 M1 (with a pin for an approval inside a `subflow`), L2 S1 (docblocks state the disclosure) and S2 above, then sends the new head. I post a new `Contract-review-claim`, the L2 reviewer reads the delta, and I read the L1 delta on the same head. The question L2 escalated, whether an earlier participant may learn a later request's status at all under the #8652 ruling, goes to the seat. Precedent: `passedSteps` (#26668) already serves an earlier step's state from the same system read.
